hypothesis: A small train-only learned similarity metric can infer candidate alias links by comparing contextual node profiles directly inside a fixed-size 576-byte state, without externally supplied candidate node-ID PAIRS, and improve typed multi-path reasoning on new identity/source seeds.

method.learned: four-weight logistic similarity over three squared feature distances
method.train: 320 historical synthetic positive/negative unrelated entity identity pairs, 420 bounded SGD epochs
method.candidate_generation: programmed enumeration of ALL possible pairwise recurrent graph edge connections; similarity decides which unmatched endpoints to associate; NO supplied candidate pair tuples
method.given_not_learned: per-node source-generated semantic profile vectors, node IDs, coded graph-edge enumeration, initial typed role and 5-weight recurrence
method.true_identity_semantics: source-generator latent shared vector for truly aliased nodes; candidate never receives whether any two IDs share latent identity

controlled_cases: main broken plus true unseen alias bridge
main broken plus unrelated bridge negative
true alias with noisy observed evidence
false alternative and necessary role damage
only main branch role changed; alternate intact

controls: learned all-pairs contextual candidate links in W22 style graph recurrence
fixed Euclidean descriptor distance < 0.045, no training
coded exact oracle using source-known identity (reference only)
